syllabus.clause: making replays safe (idempotent sinks, versioned outputs, suppressed side effects)

at.step: Predict: overwrite or version the output?
Reveal: versioned output, side effects suppressed

items.item: offsetsForTimes returns, for each partition, the earliest offset whose timestamp is greater than or equal to the target timestamp
seek overrides the fetch offsets the consumer uses on the next poll, and repeated calls for the same partition use the latest
the API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice

at.step: Reveal: versioned output, side effects suppressed

items.item: offsetsForTimes and seek are two separate steps of the same operation, not one mechanism — looking up a position by time, then actually applying it — and conflating them would misstate the real Kafka consumer API this topic draws on.

Scoping a replay to a partition or time range isn't just an optimization — it's what keeps a replay's blast radius equal to the bug's actual blast radius, rather than always equal to the whole topic's history.

The hot-log/tiered-storage/lakehouse choice this topic names is the same three-tier shape topic 8 already built for ordinary reads — replay doesn't invent a new storage hierarchy, it just reuses the existing one as a backfill source.

at.step: Reveal: where the data actually comes from

items.item: An overwritten replay output isn't just inconvenient to debug — it destroys the only evidence that could ever prove whether the replay helped, which is why versioning the output is a correctness requirement here, not a nice-to-have.

Versioned output and suppressed side effects solve two different halves of replay safety — one protects the data a replay produces, the other protects the outside world from a replay's downstream consequences — and a replay missing either half is only half safe.

at.step: Reveal: versioned output, side effects suppressed

items.item: This topic's safety mechanisms aren't new inventions — the idempotent-sink and dedup machinery from topics 12 and 13 are exactly what a versioned, side-effect-suppressing replay sink is built from, reused rather than reinvented.

at.step: Reveal: versioned output, side effects suppressed

items.item: The toy OffsetTimeIndex, ScopedReplay, BackfillSourceChooser, and overwrite/versioned sinks are deliberately simplified standalone models, not ports of any production replay tooling, and every figure shown is this run's own output, not a cited constant.

A replay being 'safe to repeat' means something stronger than 'safe to run once' — the whole point of this topic's safety machinery is that the exact same replay could be run again, by mistake or on purpose, with no different outcome.

A replay and a backfill are the same mechanism pointed at two different reasons: a replay corrects something that was processed wrong, a backfill supplies something that was never processed at all — and both draw from the same hot-log/tiered-storage/lakehouse sources.

at.step: Reveal: where the data actually comes from

items.item: Treating this topic's replay-safety guidance as a generic cross-system pattern, sourced from Stripe's API docs rather than Kafka's own, is a deliberate choice — Kafka itself has no built-in replay-safety API, so the safety burden sits entirely on how the sink and consumer are designed.

This topic's 'Lambda vs Kappa' pointer names a broader architectural choice (reprocess via a parallel batch layer versus reprocess the same streaming layer) that replay is one concrete instance of, without this topic itself teaching that comparison.
